Before reaching for a DateTimeKind, confirm DateTime is the right type: use DateOnly for a calendar date with no meaningful time (birthdates, due dates, holidays); use TimeOnly for a time of day with no meaningful date (opening hours, recurring schedule times), both need .NET 6+; use DateTimeOffset for a specific instant (timestamps, created/modified/expiration times), the preferred type for any instant. Fall back to DateTime with an explicit DateTimeKind only when none of those fit, e.g. the value crosses an API, database column, or public-contract boundary you don't control, or is a future wall-clock time whose UTC instant isn't fixed yet (then use Unspecified and say why). When DateTime is required, use Utc for instants, Unspecified only for intentional wall-clock values, and avoid Local in server code.
